findings.title: [P1] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted local URLs
findings.body: When `returnUrl` is derived from login state or a query parameter, values such as `https://attacker.example` or `//attacker.example` send authenticated users to an attacker-controlled site. Previously this argument was ignored in favor of the fixed `/dashboard` destination. Validate the URL as an allowed same-origin path before navigating.

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to logs
findings.body: Calling `recordIssuedToken` forwards the live bearer token verbatim to `console.log`. In deployments that retain or aggregate console output, anyone with log access can recover and reuse issued credentials. Audit only non-sensitive metadata or a non-reversible identifier.

findings.title: [P2] Apply the anonymous fallback after trimming blank names
findings.body: For a cached value containing only whitespace, `trim()` produces `""`, but nullish coalescing does not treat that as absent. The function consequently returns an unusable blank name rather than the fallback; check the trimmed result for emptiness before returning it.

findings.title: [P1] Restrict post-login redirects to trusted local URLs
findings.body:
If `returnUrl` originates from login state or a query parameter, values such as `https://attacker.example` or `//attacker.example` redirect authenticated users off-site, creating an open-redirect/phishing path.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to the audit log
findings.body:
Every token passed to `recordIssuedToken` is forwarded verbatim to `console.log`; in environments that retain or expose console output, anyone with log access can recover and reuse active credentials.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Apply the anonymous fallback after trimming blank names
findings.body:
For a cache entry such as `"   "`, `trim()` produces `""`, but `??` does not treat an empty string as absent. The API therefore returns an unusable blank name instead of `"Anonymous"` for this boundary input.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restrict post-login navigation to trusted same-origin URLs
findings.body:
An externally influenced `returnUrl` can redirect authenticated users to an attacker-controlled site; `javascript:` URLs can also execute script in the application origin where CSP permits them. Previously the parameter was ignored, so callers could safely pass untrusted return-state values.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Do not write issued tokens to logs
findings.body:
Calling `recordIssuedToken` with a live bearer token writes the credential verbatim to console output. Where console output is retained or collected, anyone with broader log access can recover and reuse the token until it expires.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Avoid direct console I/O on every token issuance
findings.body:
`recordIssuedToken` invokes this unconditionally for every token, writing the full token to stdout. Under high issuance rates with a synchronous or slow stdout/logging sink, these writes can block the event loop or accumulate buffered output, making authentication throughput and memory usage depend on log-consumer speed.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
